question: What does reproductive health truly mean according to the World Health Organization (WHO)?

options.A: A woman's physical capability to carry a pregnancy to full term safely
options.B: The total absence of any bacteria or viruses in the pelvic organs
options.C: The biological ability to conceive and bear children without medical help
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Think of reproductive health as more than just working body parts. The WHO looks at the whole person—physical, mental, and social well-being together! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h1)

question: As a nurse, why shouldn't you focus *only* on physical symptoms when caring for a client's reproductive health?

options.A: Because physical symptoms are rarely accurate indicators of reproductive disease
options.B: Because reproductive health includes mental, social, and bodily autonomy aspects
options.C: Because hospital policies strictly prohibit treating only physical complaints
options.D: Because laboratory tests cannot detect most reproductive system infections

explanation: You are caring for a human being, not just a body! Since reproductive health covers mental and social wellness too, great nurses look at the big picture. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the main reason pregnant women are encouraged to attend routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: To provide the mother with high doses of broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.B: To permanently prevent any potential complications during the postpartum period
options.C: To schedule the exact date and time when labor will officially begin
options.D: To monitor fetal growth and screen for conditions like anemia and high blood pressure

explanation: ANC is like a check-point for safety! It helps midwives and nurses catch small issues like low blood levels or high BP early before they become emergencies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h2)

question: A mother just gave birth six hours ago in the maternity ward. Which immediate postpartum emergency should you watch out for most closely?
explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage (heavy bleeding) is a major postpartum risk, especially in the first few hours after delivery. Always keep a close eye on your patient's lochia and vitals! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h2)

question: How do common hormonal contraceptives (like pills and injectables) mainly prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By suppressing ovulation and thickening cervical mucus
options.B: By killing the ovum before fertilization can take place
options.C: By permanently closing the fallopian tubes with scar tissue
options.D: By physically destroying sperm inside the vaginal canal

explanation: Hormones trick the body into holding back the egg (no ovulation) and make the cervical mucus too thick for swimming sperm to get through. Clever, right? [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which family planning method category also helps protect against Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)?
explanation: Only barrier methods like condoms physically block fluids, which stops both unwanted pregnancy AND pesky STIs. Pills and IUDs do not protect against infections! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h3)

question: What makes controlling Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs) so tricky in communities?

options.A: STIs cannot be transmitted if the infected person takes vitamins
options.B: Laboratory tests are completely unavailable in most health clinics
options.C: Many infections present with mild or silent symptoms
options.D: Antibiotics can cure viral infections just as easily as bacterial ones

explanation: Many STIs show zero signs at first! People feel totally fine, so they unknowingly spread the infection before realizing they need treatment. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is partner notification and treatment a must when managing STIs?

options.A: To punish individuals who engage in unprotected sexual intercourse
options.B: To determine which partner originally contracted the infection first
options.C: To prevent reinfection and break the ongoing cycle of transmission
options.D: To fulfill mandatory insurance reporting requirements for hospitals

explanation: If you treat only one partner, they will just catch the infection right back the next time they have sex. Both partners must be treated together to truly heal! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is one of the biggest roadblocks stopping teenagers from seeking reproductive health care at clinics?

options.A: Judgmental healthcare attitudes and cultural taboos
options.B: A complete lack of biological changes during puberty
options.C: Immunity to all forms of sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Strict laws requiring parental consent for all general check-ups

explanation: Too often, young people stay away from clinics because they are scared health workers will scold, judge, or gossip about them. As nurses, we must be welcoming! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h5)

question: What makes a clinic truly "youth-friendly" when it comes to reproductive health?

options.A: Programs that focus solely on treating severe physical trauma injuries
options.B: Medical facilities that treat only patients under twelve years of age
options.C: Clinics that operate exclusively during late night hours on weekends
options.D: Services that offer confidential, non-judgmental care tailored to teenagers

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics win teens' trust by keeping their business private, listening without scolding, and treating them with absolute respect. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h5)

question: After how many months of trying to conceive without success do doctors officially define infertility?
explanation: Doctors generally look at a full year (12 months) of regular, unprotected sex before starting infertility investigations. Don't panic too early! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is a very common female-related cause of infertility?

options.A: Permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: Hyperactive sperm motility within the uterus
options.C: Complete absence of the pituitary hormone testosterone
options.D: Tubal blockages from previous pelvic infections

explanation: Past untreated infections (like PID) can leave scars or blockages in the fallopian tubes, stopping the egg and sperm from meeting. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which common virus is most strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?
explanation: High-risk strains of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) are the leading cause of changes in the cervix that can lead to cancer over time. Thankfully, we have vaccines now! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of routine screening tests like the Pap smear?

options.A: To permanently cure active bacterial infections in the pelvis
options.B: To detect abnormal cellular changes before cancer develops
options.C: To prevent the initial transmission of sexually transmitted germs
options.D: To measure hormone levels during the normal menstrual cycle

explanation: Pap smears catch weird cellular changes early—long before they turn into cancer—making treatment quick and easy. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT considered a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Female genital mutilation performed without anesthesia
options.B: Forced physical practices during early puberty rites

explanation: Immunizations save children's lives from deadly diseases! They are a standard, safe medical intervention, unlike harmful cultural practices. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h8)

question: What should be your very first priority when nursing a survivor of gender-based violence?

options.A: Demanding that the survivor immediately file a police report before treatment
options.B: Providing compassionate medical care, physical safety, and emotional support
options.C: Telling the patient to forget the incident and focus on daily chores
options.D: Refusing to document physical injuries to protect the hospital from lawsuits

explanation: A survivor's safety, physical healing, and gentle emotional support always come first in clinical nursing. Make them feel safe and heard! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T3#GNS216_U1_T3_h8)
